q1_why_thumb_ip_spread_over_the_thumb.mechanism: R1's `THUMB DISTAL OWNERSHIP GUARD` predicate is INVERTED.  It fires when `arc_of(THUMB,v) <= XIJ['THUMB'][2] + tau`, but XIJ['THUMB'][2] is the arc position of the IP JOINT measured from the CMC head, i.e. the DISTAL end of the MCP segment.  Every thumb-owned vertex satisfies that inequality (all of them have arc <= IP-joint arc), so the guard becomes 'THUMB_IP_R >= 2 x sum(others)' over the ENTIRE thumb: distal phalanx, proximal phalanx, first metacarpal and thumb base.  The intended predicate was distal-of-IP: `arc >= XIJ['THUMB'][2] - tau`.

q2_which_semantic_term_caused_the_spread.answer: the semantic guard (THUMB DISTAL OWNERSHIP GUARD), not the lateral distance term, not the normalisation order
details: the guard sets raw[THUMB_IP_R] = max(raw, 2*others) BEFORE normalisation; the normalisation is a plain partition and cannot undo it (it scales numerator and denominator together)
there is NO else-branch that restricts THUMB_IP_R to the distal phalanx, so once the predicate is always true the distal authority becomes a whole-digit authority
the longitudinal term lam = exp(-((xi-mj)/kappa)^2) and the lateral term mu = exp(-(d/L0)^2) are both computed and then OVERRIDDEN by the guard on every thumb-owned vertex

the region mask is too wide in an independent way: OWN_V is a plain nearest-chain partition with NO thenar / first-metacarpal-base region, so the whole thumb base is classified as THUMB and inherits the same treatment
the R1 audit defect (below) then hid the symptom: violations were reported as []
q2_which_semantic_term_caused_the_spread.normalisation_order: normalise -> prune(4) -> normalise; deterministic and NOT the cause (worst normalisation error 4.4e-8)

q3_why_first_web_violations_empty_while_.r1_mask_rule: d_poly(thumb chain) <= 2*median_edge AND d_poly(index chain) <= 2*median_edge  (no longitudinal (arc) bound at all)
q3_why_first_web_violations_empty_while_.audit_bug: the R1 audit violation loop exempted THUMB_IP_R / INDEX_PIP_R / INDEX_DIP_R explicitly (`if b not in WEB_OK and b not in (...)`), so a THUMB_IP entry in the first web could never be reported as a violation while the declared whitelist was WEB_OK only -> audit semantics and weight semantics disagree
q3_why_first_web_violations_empty_while_.build_bug: the R1 web branch removed THUMB_IP only when `i not in NAIL_THUMB_V`; every thumb nail vertex that also fell inside the first-web band kept THUMB_IP allowed AND had it forced to >= 2x others -> non-zero THUMB_IP inside the web

q4_why_cmc_and_mcp_max_are_small.statement: because the guard forces THUMB_IP_R >= 2 x sum(everything else) on every thumb-owned vertex, the remaining groups can only share at most 1/3 of the normalised weight; THUMB_CMC_R and THUMB_MCP_R then split that 1/3 between themselves, which caps them at ~0.3618 / ~0.2955.  The weakness is a SYMPTOM of the inverted guard, not an independent defect.
q4_why_cmc_and_mcp_max_are_small.expected_after_fix: with a joint-local partition of unity along the thumb arc the first-metacarpal band and the proximal-phalanx band reach THUMB_CMC_R / THUMB_MCP_R dominance on their own surface, without any artificial >0.5 gate

q5_root_cause_classification.audit_semantic_mismatch: PRIMARY (confirmed: audit exempts THUMB_IP from the violation check while declaring a whitelist that excludes it)

geodesic_coordinate_rejection.statement: geodesic distance from the thumb distal-most vertex is NOT monotone along the digit on this mesh: the thumb NAIL plate and the adjacent dorsal sheet are 148-180 mm away in surface distance while only 8-30 mm away in space.  R1 nevertheless seeded GEO at the distal-most vertex and defined gval(); that coordinate was never used by the R1 guards, so it caused no damage - but it is UNUSABLE for R1A and is explicitly rejected.
